evidence.claim: The Gunflint Trail winds 57 paved miles from Grand Marais on Lake Superior to Saganaga Lake near the Canadian border.
evidence.quote: The 57-mile-long paved road winds its way from Grand Marais on the north shore of Lake Superior, to Saganaga Lake near the Canadian border.

evidence.claim: A National Scenic Byway since 2009, it crosses the Superior National Forest.
evidence.quote: The road was designated a National Scenic Byway in 2009.

evidence.claim: A National Scenic Byway since 2009, it crosses the Superior National Forest.
evidence.quote: The pastoral landscape of the Superior National Forest is a quiet nature destination

evidence.claim: The Federal Highway Administration highlights Lake Superior views and a changing forest, from deciduous trees through conifers to boreal woods.
evidence.quote: Travel the Gunflint Trail and experience views of beautiful Lake Superior

evidence.claim: The Federal Highway Administration highlights Lake Superior views and a changing forest, from deciduous trees through conifers to boreal woods.
evidence.quote: The forest changes from mixed deciduous to maple, to mixed conifer, to conifer, and to boreal forest

evidence.claim: The route began as a footpath linking inland lakes with Lake Superior.
evidence.quote: Originally a footpath for travelers from inland lakes to Lake Superior

evidence.claim: Cook County widened it into a dirt road in the 1890s to support the Paulson Mine.
evidence.quote: The footpath was improved into a dirt road by Cook County in the 1890s to support the Paulson Mine.

evidence.claim: Local business owners paid for improvements in the 1920s.
evidence.quote: In the 1920s, local business owners paid for some improvements to the road; by 1957, it was paved from Grand Marais to Hungry Jack Lake.

evidence.claim: In 1929, the road was extended north to Saganaga Lake to serve construction of Chik Wauk and Sea Gull lodges, tying its growth to tourism.
evidence.quote: In 1929, in order to facilitate the construction of both Chik Wauk and the nearby Sea Gull Lodge, the Gunflint Trail was extended northwards by several miles to connect with Saganaga Lake.

evidence.claim: By 1957, pavement reached Hungry Jack Lake from Grand Marais.
evidence.quote: by 1957, it was paved from Grand Marais to Hungry Jack Lake.

evidence.claim: The final gravel section, south of Sea Gull Lake, was paved in 1979.
evidence.quote: The last gravel section, south of Sea Gull Lake, was paved in 1979.

evidence.claim: From Highway 61 in Grand Marais, drive north to Northern Light Lake, then northwest along the Brule River.
evidence.quote: The route begins at Highway 61 in Grand Marais. It travels generally northward until Northern Light Lake, where it turns northwestward, following the Brule River.

evidence.claim: Beyond the river crossing, the road follows Swamper Creek and bends west along Poplar Lake, passing Birch, Mayhew and Loon lakes before the Gunflint Lake access roads.
evidence.quote: It crosses the Brule and continues north-northwest along Swamper Creek, gradually arcing westward and running along the northern shore of Poplar Lake. The road continues west past several lakes including Birch, Mayhew, and Loon before reaching the access roads to Gunflint Lake.

evidence.claim: It turns north near Round Lake, then west at Sea Gull Lake to end at Saganaga.
evidence.quote: The route turns north near Round Lake and travels several miles to Sea Gull Lake, where it turns west again to its terminus at Saganaga Lake.

evidence.claim: FHWA advises at least two hours for the trip, including the return along the same road.
evidence.quote: The trip requires at least two hours, as you will have to return to Grand Marais by the same route.

evidence.claim: Pincushion Mountain offers a view back toward the water the Gunflint Trail leaves behind.
evidence.quote: From atop Pincusion Mountain one has a panoramic view of the Sawtooth Mountains, Lake Superior, and the town, harbor, and lighthouse of Grand Marais.

evidence.claim: Pincushion Mountain offers a view back toward the water the Gunflint Trail leaves behind.
evidence.quote: Originally a footpath for travelers from inland lakes to Lake Superior

evidence.claim: The peak belongs to the Sawtooth Mountains, beside the Lake Superior boundary of Cook County.
evidence.quote: Pincushion Mountain is a peak in the Sawtooth Mountains near the midpoint of the southern boundary of Cook County, which is formed by the north shore of Lake Superior.

evidence.claim: From its summit, the view includes the mountain range, Lake Superior, and the town, harbor and lighthouse of Grand Marais.
evidence.quote: From atop Pincusion Mountain one has a panoramic view of the Sawtooth Mountains, Lake Superior, and the town, harbor, and lighthouse of Grand Marais.

evidence.claim: Hungry Jack Lake marked a stage in the gradual paving of the Gunflint Trail: by 1957, pavement extended here from Grand Marais.
evidence.quote: by 1957, it was paved from Grand Marais to Hungry Jack Lake.

evidence.claim: The lake covers 463 acres and reaches a maximum depth of 71 feet, at an elevation of 1,680 feet.
evidence.quote: The lake is 463 acres (1.87 km2) with a maximum depth of 71 feet (22 m) and found at an elevation of 1,680 feet (510 m).

evidence.claim: The lake was putatively named for Anderson Jackson Scott, a surveyor's assistant temporarily without food supplies here.
evidence.quote: Hungry Jack Lake was putatively named for Anderson Jackson Scott, a surveyor's assistant who at this lake was temporarily without food supplies.

evidence.claim: At Saganaga, the road reaches a lake shared by Minnesota and Ontario.
evidence.quote: its terminus at Saganaga Lake.

evidence.claim: At Saganaga, the road reaches a lake shared by Minnesota and Ontario.
evidence.quote: Saganaga Lake is a large lake on the Minnesota – Ontario international border.

evidence.claim: Its name comes from an Ojibwe term meaning Lake of Many Islands.
evidence.quote: Its name comes from an Ojibwe term meaning Lake of Many Islands.

evidence.claim: Most of the lake lies within the Boundary Waters Canoe Area Wilderness, Quetico Provincial Park and La Verendrye Provincial Park.
evidence.quote: Most of the lake is protected by the Boundary Waters Canoe Area Wilderness in the United States and by Quetico Provincial Park and La Verendrye Provincial Park in Canada.

evidence.claim: Overlooking it is Chik Wauk Lodge, a rough-cut stone building constructed in 1933 and used since 2010 as a museum and nature center.
evidence.quote: It overlooks Saganaga Lake.

evidence.quote: Since 2010, Chik Wauk has been run as a museum and nature center

evidence.claim: The lodge building has not been significantly altered since its original construction.
evidence.quote: The building has not been significantly altered since its original construction in 1933.

evidence.claim: The stone lodge was once the center of a fishing resort, offering cabins and meals as well as access to the lakes.
evidence.quote: was once the centerpiece of a large Gunflint Trail resort complex, which offered to tourists: lodging in rustic-style cabins, cooked meals as well as access to above-average fishing and northern Minnesota scenery.

flags: Pincushion Mountain and Hungry Jack Lake moments are shorter because their cache pages contain little descriptive evidence.
Pincushion hike distance is supported only by Wikipedia; omitted the current three-mile drive and nine-mile hike pending a trail-manager source.
Material strip mileage runs toward Grand Marais; moments instead follow the explicitly described Grand Marais-to-Saganaga drive, reversing that mileage direction.
Saganaga page gives a 280-foot maximum but says the deepest point is outside the BWCA; omitted depth to avoid conflating lake and wilderness boundaries.
Cache uses both Ojibwa and Ojibwe; retained Ojibwe for the Saganaga name as in its source.
